reading.title: Learning from the first farmers
reading.text: Indigenous communities manage around a quarter of the world's land, and their territories often contain more wildlife than national parks. In my opinion, governments have been far too slow to recognise this. Traditional knowledge, passed down through generations, includes ingenious methods of farming without chemicals. Some scientists dismiss this knowledge as unscientific, but genetic studies have shown that indigenous crops are often more resistant to drought. Rich countries should be more generous in funding these communities, rather than imposing their own solutions.

items.s: Governments have acted quickly to support indigenous land management.
Traditional farming methods can be very clever.
Wealthy nations ought to give more money to indigenous communities.
